instruction: Duplicate slide 12 and insert the copy immediately after it.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires duplicating slide 12 and inserting after it. Verified: Original has 24 slides, after duplication should have 25. Slides at positions 11 and 12 (0-indexed, which are slides 12 and 13 in 1-indexed) should be identical.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for correct slide count (25), 0.5 for slides 12 and 13 being identical

llm_judge_reasons: Text-only comparison is semantically insufficient for verifying slide duplication - only checks text content, not images, formatting, layouts, backgrounds, animations, or non-text shapes
A true 'duplicate slide' should be an exact replica including all visual elements, but getter only extracts and compares text from shapes
Shape order dependency: comparison uses list equality which requires same order - functionally identical slides with reordered shapes would incorrectly fail
Correct coverage: evaluator checks both slide count increase (24→25) and consecutive slide identity (positions 11-12)
Correct index translation: properly translates user-facing 'slide 12' (1-indexed) to positions 11-12 (0-indexed)
Proper postconfig: saves file to ensure getter reads updated state
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace text-only comparison with comprehensive slide comparison: use python-pptx's slide XML or serialize entire slide structure (shapes, positions, sizes, colors, images, etc.)
Consider comparing slide XML representation: prs.slides[pos]._element for exact structural match
Alternative: Hash slide binary representation or compare all shape properties (type, position, size, fill, line, text formatting)
For robust duplication check: verify shape count, shape types, positions, text content, images, and formatting all match
Make shape comparison order-independent if order doesn't matter, or explicitly verify shape order is preserved in duplication
